View attachment 3681407

The thing about them returning to form:
View attachment 3681416
So yeah, there's a lot going on here. And people that could or could not be in control of Ami sometimes. She also seems to disagree with voices in her head a lot. Which, added to the thing about Akira receiving psychosis from his father, could also relate to Ami receiving it from Akira (by being his daughter). So it could range from a deal to simply hereditary mental issues.

At the very least someone opposed to Pareidolia that wants to return to form exists. Someone that apparently cares for Akira too and is taking the form of Ami.

Edit: on a minor note, she does mention sacrifices, and has an obsession about asking if other girls would be willing to kill and be killed for Akira, and given that she was sacrificed/murdered before him getting comatose, maybe she did offer herself as a sacrifice who knows.
Click to expand...
There's also how sickness seems to be mentioned a lot in relation to Pareidolia. The Pareidolia Mall and Amy stuff was apparently surrounded by sickness:
Amy - "The world outside these walls is contaminated. Breathing in the air for longer than three minutes will fill your lungs with some weird stuff and then you die."
- "Watch your step. If you cut your feet on broken glass, they could get infected. Then, you'll have to go all the way to the medical ward. And they pretty much always have really long lines."
- "Me? I could never. I have a degenerative bone disease and my doctor says extreme sports aren't good for me. But I do know of a shop here that sells them if you want to try!"
Amy seems like a contaminated Ami that's basically falling apart mentally and physically.

She also doesn't have hands:
Amy - "Teehee! You should have seen me when I still had hands."
Which makes me wonder if Ami was referring to chopping her own hands off recently, after hurting Sensei. Ami seems to think she deserves to be hurt:
Ami - "Do you want to hurt me to make up for it? Because you can if you want. I deserve it."

The 'Amy' Happy Event may have been foreshadowing things to come. Even the Dad stuff:
Amy - "Hahah! Will do. You wanna know what kind of vibes you give off, though?"
- "Dad vibes."

That may have been answered in the 'Amy' Happy Event:
Sensei - "Are you still in touch with your mom?"
Amy - 'I am! We meet up on Wednesdays to go water the plants and have our retinal fluid refilled over in the medical ward."

I wouldn't blame Ami for choosing her Mom over Sensei.

How Sensei has treated her:
Ami - "I think you've got it backwards. I won't be able to follow you if you keep trying to break my kneecaps. And that's exactly what you're doing right now."
Sensei Narrator - "I've spent time with two families who would openly allow me to insert myself into them (in any way I want) while neglecting the family I already have for reasons I can't even properly explain."
Niki - "That son of a fucking bitch. Who does he think he is just disappearing and leaving you to fend for yourself like this? And why the fuck won't he answer his phone?" (He's too busy preparing to fuck one of her best friends.)
How Sekai treated her:
Ami - "Granted, I was always more of a mama's girl in the first place."
- "And the way she treated me..."
- "It was like nothing else mattered to her."
If Sensei actually starts prioritizing Ami, then things may be different.

Ami might as well be the Harley Quinn to Sensei's Joker, though, tbh.

posts.content_html_raw:
I was rewatching the conversation between Karin and Akira after the karaoke. I know we have all said something about how Karin didn't deserve what happened and how Pareidolia is a piece of shit. But I don't recall if we have said enough about how Akira has grown.
The need to apologise


Then actually doing it just a week later


I mean, obviously he's not a selfless or actual good person - he's still a self-centered piece of shit, but compared to how he dealt with the Molly stuff (which was just letting her do everything) this is leaps and bounds better.

also this is very funny



Finally, and I think this exemplifies his growth a lot, Akira comes as clean as he could without sounding insane and gives her an out like he's never given anyone else:
He really explains stuff and gives her closure, it's amazing now that I'm rewatching it after replaying the game from start to current update. Old Akira would never have been able to do anything like this, or even cared to.

Then they say a lot of stuff and Karin goes:
And the first time I read this I was really sad. But now I feel strangely proud. See, yes, he's nothing like the image that Karin had, but that image was her fault sort of. Akira was never that and he was never going to be that. Evidence was all around her and she chose not to see.

However, the Akira that we see in this conversation is WAY more than the man he was. He could have easily manipulated her and given her the answers she wanted, and yet he gives it to her straight and leaves the option for her just to be done with him. Actual growth.

Beautiful yet tragic foreshadowing for what would eventually come for Maya... To those who found Akira's reaction to Maya disappearing rushed, I urge them to look at scenes like this one again. The pieces were being laid out an entire chapter in advance:

Sensei - "Do you really think there's a chance you might... "go away?""
Maya - "..."

First of all, welcome. Secondly, I'd prefer for it to be Himawari, that was my first assumption when rewarching the event - it's the return to form that I have problem with I guess.

Sekai's return seems to be one of the longest and most important arcs in the game. I'm unsure who else's return to form would it be, especially because it's said that Akira wants it with that exact expression.

For the sake of argument, it could Maya's prime return to form. This is one for the wild theory corner right next to the identity of so many narrators since some of them seem to speak from the future, and some from the present.

A boring answer would be the return to form for both Ami and Akira (which seems to be happening in update 0.40), or even that Ami is one of the narrators (less boring) - which is also a theory, be it the Mega Ami, or even her being the world itself since it seems that Ami being left alone in a doomed world is a common theme.

Of course a problem with all of that is that the narrator that stops the auto-mode says that "wires can only take you so far" or something. And I can't remember anyone else other than Sekai being involved with Wires in a way that would invoke that comment.

If I recall correctly, Sekai's return seems to have been an effort started by Wires with the recovery of Akira's memories (she shows up as a shadow during the flashback). But then her actual return happens during summer (in which she seems to have saved Akira), and is only in spring that she's showing up all the time.

And a last one that I don't really buy, but for the sake of inclusion: I haven't organized it yet, but I have found some evidence to suggest that Akira and Sekai (or one of the Sekais) might have been fused. AmIOKay refers to Akira as Sekai at one point, there have been narrators that confused themselves with Akira himself saying things like "I, no, I mean him", and the general understanding that Sekai has always been following him - or maybe that simply her influence on him was so great that a part of him became her reflection idk - my point is that there is also a possibility that "us" could simply be the royal we, indicating both Sekai and Akira as parts of the same being.

Sure she may be annoying at times, but I still can't help but feel bad for Tsukasa here... and honestly just in general.

Tsukasa - "Can you teach me how to play this game now?"
Sensei - "Immediately after insulting me?"

Some Random Sekai stuff for those interested, since I just felt compelled to do this:
Sekai as Teacher has been around since the 1st Happy Event 'The Room With Clocks':
Teacher/Sekai - "I decided to clock in early today so I could give you a very special lesson before my next appearance in chapter two!"
And may have been alive(?) since the 2nd Happy Event: https://lessonsinlove.wiki/index.php?title=II
The voices saying: "Albatross. Guardian. Aluminum. Iodine. Nylon. Severance. Happenstance. Entry. Lovers. Incest. Virtual. Emaciated. Sadness. The answer you seek is hope."

Which can translate to: "A.g.a.i.n. S.h.e. L.i.v.e.s, the answer you seek is HOPE." Assuming the "She" here is Sekai. (AmIOkay Maya is being crucified and there's times she's hung herself, so I'm still on the fence on whether it's Sekai or Maya that Yasu implies HOPE brought back.)

Nevertheless, like Sekai's Chapter 2 'Something Everyone Knows And Ignores' Happy Event, aka S.E.K.A.I, this Acronym theme seems to be implied to be her thing in particular.

And she was presumably narrating in the: https://lessonsinlove.wiki/index.php?title=O_World_(In_Our_Final_Moments)
Chapter 1 Main Event, as the Narrator in it seems to be her:
Narrator/Sekai (?) - "But I'll always be watching, okay?"
- "Goodnight...Sensei..."
White Dress Sekai - "I know. I've been watching. I'm always watching. That's how the whole 'being dead' thing works."
Restored Sekai - "ISN'T THAT RIGHT-"
- "AKIRA???????"
Assuming that that "Sensei" is actually just Sensei replacing "Akira" with it, due to this taking place long before he started acknowledging his name as pointed out by Noriko:
Sensei - "Then...why have you kept calling me Sensei this whole time?"
Noriko - "I...haven't?"
- "That makes...basically no sense at all. Are you sure you're not just...overlooking it? Like how you apparently were all of the times I've called you Akira?"
(Ironically Sensei's name was revealed by Sekai in the Chapter 3 Main Event 'Smells of Summer' which mostly involved Noriko)

Sekai also seems to have been the Narrator in:https://lessonsinlove.wiki/index.php?title=Imaginary_Veins
In Chapter 3:
Narrator/Sekai - "Rapist! Lecher! Pedophile! Flay her 'till she's DEAD!"
- "The things they'd say if only they could see inside my head."
- "IT'S STILL ME. IT HAS ALWAYS BEEN ME. IT WILL ALWAYS BE ME."
- "I MISS YOU SO MUCH."
Background - "TURN AROUND YOU FUCKING COWARD
DIG ME UP, I MISS YOU
IT'S FINE IF WE JUST PLAY PRETEND
IGNORE THE FRAYING SINEW
THE NERVES STILL WORK! MY BRAIN IS FINE!
OUR THREADS CAN STAND THE TEST!
ALIVE! IN LOVE! AS BROKEN BIRDS!
JUST ONE HASN'T LEFT THE NEST - ME"
Also may be the Narrator in Haruka's Chapter 3: https://lessonsinlove.wiki/index.php?title=Again,_I_Can't_Recall
Albeit, this is simply based off them reading a poem by Sekai. Probably is the Narrator in other events, but one can only guess.

Sekai's shadow actually first (?) showed up in Ami's Chapter 1 'Cute Girls and Stuff':
Ami - "Yup! I'm a mind reader. And right now, you're thinking that you want to take me shopping."
Although, it may have been sooner. This shadow later shows up in Chapter 2's 'Spotless Mind' Main Event:
Noriko - "You're such a good boy."
Yasu has also noted that "the world itself" speaks under the cover of shadows:
Yasu - "It speaks through the wind, backwards and under the cover of shadows. The same language the cicadas speak."
Among other things, so this "the world itself" that comes up, may either be Sekai, a Sekai, or related to Sekai. Sekai translating to World is unlikely to be a coincidence. Yasu's Chapter 3: https://lessonsinlove.wiki/index.php?title=The_River_Styx

If it's the former, they would have to reset (a proper reset including Akira) - which, granted, they seemed to have tried to two times during summer. The first time being stopped (probably) by Sekai, and the second one (probably) by Pareidolia (since Yasu seemed certain that Akira was going to be factory reset). If it's the latter then we're going into the endgame for everyone involved, whatever that means I have no idea. I agree. I feel like that during the first chapter a lot of the Happy Events seem to support this, in the sense that there is "a Maya" (AmIOkay) with him in the room with the clocks and more or less out of the current timeline (also during other Happy Events). The recurring flash of a Maya entity waiting for him at the end of a white corridor could also suggest this.

And more from a storytelling perspective, while Sekai currently brings the entire timeline together, she's a controversial, if not malevolent being. I feel like there's something to be gained from a more "positive" figure also tying everything together so that there's more than one choice by the end (which Maya prime would be if she remained as one of the narrators, still searching and trying to protect him after her reset), not to count the enormous payoff from her reveal as both still alive and present in the entire game (but hidden as a narrator).

Of course, what I just said about Maya could also be applied to Ami. Being Sekai's daughter she would serve a somewhat similar role as an alternate figure present throughout but of a different and more positive tone than her mother. I don't really buy the narrative of Himawari being the narrator that seems in love with Akira (while she is obviously a narrator at certain points). Unless Himawari is also either Ami or Maya, but that would be even more out of left field. I think it's more likely that one of the narrators simply is Ami or Maya - and between them Maya seems the more likely also.

So we had a bit of a talk about what was written next to Himawari on, i guess it was a wooden desk, in hexdec some while ago, the Infant Joy poem.
That event was for me the time that i decided that Himawari was the most likely name for her.
This is pretty much me repeating myself, because i posted this some months ago, but since we have "new" people here, why not.

The pretty much 100% for me was already -- q "Your little sunflower." -- Where q is a ren'py "sayer" shown as "???", which is most of the time the entity we/i name Himawari.
(Just did a quick and dirty search with np++ and this seems to be in the "Flowerchild" Event, while i don't know what kind of event that is (Main/Character/Happy)).
But "q" is also used for entities we dont know yet, so little chance i might be off.

Still..., we have HimawariCo. There to help or whatever, which seems to describe her character.

Back to the poem.
The poem is called Infant Joy by William Blake.
It has a second part that i think is not in the game.
Further, the poem is a contra to another poem by William Blake called "Infant Sadness".

So two things come to mind.
The poem is supposed to be interpreted together with its missing part and it's contra.
And i don't know what to make of that.
Or, the part "Joy is my name" is to be taken literally.

For that we would have to dive a bit into "Hanakotoba", which is the japanese flower language.
Sunflower/Himawari "CAN" be interpreted as Joy, while... that counts for a lot of flowers in western and japanese flower language. It's kind of what can be associated with flowers in general.
Normally Sunflowers in japanese are more linked to loyalty, longevity and respect.

But flowers seem to play at least some role in LIL.

We have Sekai (Cherry Blossom), Ayane (Daisy/Sunflower) and "Himawari" (Sunflower?).
The thing with Ayane is that i can't tell if her flower pattern dress is daisy or sunflower, because they can be hard to tell apart given that they can look alike, more so if it's orange Daisies.

I forgot what Daisies mean in "Hanakotaba", but i found it very interesting that sakura tree's/cherry blossom, can mean "Hope" in Hanakotaba.
Which, if flower language has some meaning in LiL, would relate Sekai to the entity we know as Hope.

posts.content_html_raw:
I guess i could try to give some instructions on np++, so more peeps can go wild.



So yeah this is german, not russian. So roman/latin, meaning there are similarities. Try to figure them out.

What you wanne go for is "Suchen" (search) (top toolbar). Search will give you a dropdown with (among others) "Search in files" which will open the dialog top right.
Selected tab in dialog (top right sub window) is "In dateien suchen" (Search in files).
Suche nach (Search for), i entered "Voices". You can put looots of stuff in there. Can get complicated. A one word search is ofc easy. Rule of thump. The simpler your search string, the more results you get.
So in the end it's about building good search strings.
Filter (yeah same in both languages) You can specifiy here which extensions to include, or, i guess which to omit. Kind of vice versa. I chose to only include .rpy files. Should be obvious. (wildcard * for all rpy files)
Verzeichniss (Folder). Should be self explaining.
Checkmark "Unterverzeichnisse" (Include subdirectories). Yeah we want that.

Suchergebnissse (Search results) in this case 46. Header of bottom section.
Zeile (Line) 4321 gave it away.
Also shows in which .rpy file i found what i was searching for. In this case "finalwarning.rpy"

At the start:
Doesn't matter which .rpy file you open initially. In fact you could open any file in the lil directory, or even elsewhere, as long as you set your search directory properly.
Normally i open Ami's script file to start, because it's the first .rpy file at the top in explorer.

Left part of my screenshot is screens.rpy.
If you click a line in the search results (bottom), you open the file that has that line of text, at the right(meaning correct) line.
There you scroll up till you get the system label/variable (forkin phyton) of the event. In this case it was resetsix3.
To get the actual ingame event name, you search for the label-/variablename (resetsix3) in all files.
It will show you a result in screens.rpy. Click it, and in the line with "textbutton _", you'll see the actual event name.

I hope that helps.
I'll answer questions should they arise.

joryuken said:
question for all you theorist out there, would it be possible that at the end of all the resets the mayas that ended up going away, be part of the original? like little fragments, that are just trying to come together as one?
Click to expand...
Considering "removed" memories tend to resurface through dreams for Makoto, Tsuneyo, and seemingly Sensei at least, it's likely possible.

Tsuneyo is definitely more of an oddity, but she at least seemed to recall hearing about the resets before hearing about them in this timeline:
Tsuneyo - "I'm confused about that myself. I understand how irrational this all is, but I can't help but feel like it's not my first time hearing it."
And recalled being there to hear Sensei say something she wasn't there for, in this timeline:
Sensei - "No...I mean that you weren't there when I said that."
Tsuneyo - "How could I possibly remember something I was not there to hear?"

Tsuneyo seemed to be recalling memories from past Tsuneyos through dreams that current Tsuneyo has, and it seems to be something she was unaware she was doing:
Tsuneyo - "The problem is that I have never been here before. I've only seen this place in dreams --- so the act of retracing anything seems difficult."
- "And it must be true as I've been seeing this very image in my sleep. Being up here on this metal wheel with you. I see it sometimes when I blink too."
Sensei - "You're remembering something you're not supposed to remember. But I don't know why you're remembering it and that...is confusing to me. But we can try and figure that out later."

Overall: Based off Sensei having to mention the ferris wheel and talk to Tsuneyo about it before she started recalling things, Sensei probably needs to take New Maya to the festival on her bday, carry boxes with/for her, or maybe have a picnic on the roof. Then Maya Prime memories may start being recalled by New Maya.

Or it could imply that Maya Prime truly is gone. Only time will tell.

It also seems like a painful process, which would probably cause most to fight against remembering things even if they could. Which makes me recall what Maya once said:
Maya - "I mean...Would you be able to handle the memories of hundreds of thousands of lifetimes if they were to all rush in at once?"

When it comes to Maya Prime at least, she may have had Millions of years worth of memory (and suffering), so I'm not sure what would happen if it all came back immediately, or how long it'd take for a Maya to be a "Maya Prime" considering just how much more memories that version would have had, and what would be required to recall them.

Edit: If you simply meant whether or not there might be a Maya being used as a core for the creation of all the Mayas in the resets, then I'm not sure. The actual girls could be elsewhere acting more as templates for the girls that share their shapes, hence the recent Template9 stuff in regards to Nao-chan. There also was how it seemed implied New Maya was a "Prototype":
Maya 2 - "This melon is reserved for THE PROTOTYPE. Please return the melon and await THE PROTOTYPE."
Unless the melon was for someone/thing else.

Yes, that theory has been out there for as long as i know, while i brought that up too.
In reality there could be just a handfull of characters that are real and the majority of the girls could just be fragments of those.
Or even fragments of Akira.

There's just no real evidence for that.
Besides, again, floor 2 was no meant to be. Those girls (+additional side characters) where a patreon stretch goal.
And one has to keep that in mind. Because the story must still be coherent if there were only 10 girls + side characters.
So to give that theory any value it would have to be broken down to the original 10 girls and side characters.
Meaning, focusing if that would make sense for those 10 and side characters.
Who could be a fragment of who if it's only 10+.

Now we have a cast of 20+.
So the likeliness some characters are shards or derivations of others rose significantly.
The point here is to discern if some girls are shards/fragments in a supernatural way, or if they are "just" character derivations with less meaning.

Another thing i wanted to add in general.
While it is possible that all Maya's we know might be part of an original Maya, the way how some of them are pretty deformed makes me think.
As i see it, it might be Sel's interpretation, meaning, what false common sense would tell people, how offspring of incestuous relationships would have to look like.
Don't want to go to deep because tl;dr but, just because you have a kid with your brother/sister or whatever, doesn't make it look like Frankenstein's Monster.
Impairing it's imune system though, that's more likely.

So what I think the otherworldly Mayas are, is that they are offspring of an original Maya (which does not forcefully mean old or new Maya) and offspring of the offspring.
Meaning during all those cycles where Maya had sex with not 100% Akira, she got pregnant.
Which might have led to "AmIOkay".
Then Akira had a kid with AmIOkay (Daughter) which led to Long Maya (Grand daughter), then with Long Maya which made Moyo and so on.
We have scenes where Akira has some kind of sex or "dna" transmission with the otherworldly Mayas already in the game.

What we do know (most likely) is that Akira has a daughter with Ayane. Presumably "Himawari".
But Ayane, as far as we know, never gave birth to Himawari, at least not that we saw.
The point here might be that Akira's offspring might get "harvested" at some point, we don't get to see.
Which might even be a purpose of Kumon'mi, or the gods need to feel, through Akira.

This might also tie in with how Himawari was enlisted as a "freelancer", which could also apply to the Mayas.
Harvested as childs of Akira from Kumon'mi and enlisted to help inside Kumon'mi, at the point they are ready to do so.

A more funny anecdote to add here.
What was it called? The "Untitled Children Show"?
Maybe it's not the show thats untitled, but the Maya's inside of it.
Making it the "Show of unnamed kids of Akira". While they do have names, just none that their father gave them.

Yes, that theory has been out there for as long as i know, while i brought that up too.
In reality there could be just a handfull of characters that are real and the majority of the girls could just be fragments of those.
Or even fragments of Akira.
There's just no real evidence for that.
Besides, again, floor 2 was no meant to be. Those girls (+additional side characters) where a patreon stretch goal.
And one has to keep that in mind. Because the story must still be coherent if there were only 10 girls + side characters.
So to give that theory any value it would have to be broken down to the original 10 girls and side characters.
Meaning, focusing if that would make sense for those 10 and side characters.
Who could be a fragment of who if it's only 10+.
Now we have a cast of 20+.
So the likeliness some characters are shards or derivations of others rose significantly.
The point here is to discern if some girls are shards/fragments in a supernatural way, or if they are "just" character derivations with less meaning.
Another thing i wanted to add in general.
While it is possible that all Maya's we know might be part of an original Maya, the way how some of them are pretty deformed makes me think.
As i see it, it might be Sel's interpretation, meaning, what false common sense would tell people, how offspring of incestuous relationships would have to look like.
Don't want to go to deep because tl;dr but, just because you have a kid with your brother/sister or whatever, doesn't make it look like Frankenstein's Monster.
Impairing it's imune system though, that's more likely.
So what I think the otherworldly Mayas are, is that they are offspring of an original Maya (which does not forcefully mean old or new Maya) and offspring of the offspring.
Meaning during all those cycles where Maya had sex with not 100% Akira, she got pregnant.
Which might have led to "AmIOkay".
Then Akira had a kid with AmIOkay (Daughter) which led to Long Maya (Grand daughter), then with Long Maya which made Moyo and so on.
We have scenes where Akira has some kind of sex or "dna" transmission with the otherworldly Mayas already in the game.
What we do know (most likely) is that Akira has a daughter with Ayane. Presumably "Himawari".
But Ayane, as far as we know, never gave birth to Himawari, at least not that we saw.
The point here might be that Akira's offspring might get "harvested" at some point, we don't get to see.
Which might even be a purpose of Kumon'mi, or the gods need to feel, through Akira.
This might also tie in with how Himawari was enlisted as a "freelancer", which could also apply to the Mayas.
Harvested as childs of Akira from Kumon'mi and enlisted to help inside Kumon'mi, at the point they are ready to do so.
A more funny anecdote to add here.
What was it called? The "Untitled Children Show"?
Maybe it's not the show thats untitled, but the Maya's inside of it.
Making it the "Show of unnamed kids of Akira". While they do have names, just none that their father gave them.

posts.content_html_raw:
I feel like everyone has pointed out good enough reasons for people to jump ship - it's just that, and I'm sure I'm preaching to the choir here, since we're all still playing the game - but maybe they thought of LiL as a different kind of story?
A dude that was abused as a child, made his predator/first love his world, so that he wouldn't have to deal with his mother issues. When that world died he completely broke and dealt it with (by not dealing with it) by using a child sexually as a crutch (Maya - which seems to have been ""consensual"", if not initiated by her, which is hinted at many times, especially when Noriko says that by her doing it (?) she broke him even more). Then as the resets begin, there's this entire chatroom of gods and supernatural entities intent on having him have his way with real/but also not real reflections of a game/not game... I mean, really? In this context, does anything really surprise anyone?

Cause as I see it, LiL is not a "porn game" in the sense of what people generally expect of this genre. It is a very fucked up story of a broken person, groomed by a predator, that tries to become better and yet everytime he does the world smacks him in the head. And yet through all this crap we have some moments like his smile having Ami as a daughter and it makes it somehow worth it.

I mean, I just don't know - if it was just a fantasy-fullfilment porn game I'd totally understand it being just another tag someone wouldn't want, but in the context of this story/Akira not being the player, and having to play for about 3 weeks of story until the Tsukasa thing even "happens" (cause nothing happened at this point actually), I also feel it's a bit weird. It's uncomfortable for me, but it's also kind of expected to be honest.

I feel personally that LiL is a kind of "can a person as damaged as this recover? and if so, how and to what extent?" I feel like what Akira did before the resets is not something that would make him completely outside of redemption (if he even is still alive after all of this). And the nature of cycles themselves seem to open the opportunity for all of this to not really count in the "real world" in the first place.

From a narrative angle, it seems convenient that all the fucked up shit Akira did is within an ever repeating cycle that even if it's real it's also somehow not. And the only real crime he did before is heavily hinted to have been initiated by his "victim", and maybe even kept going by her as well, while he was more or less a husk of having his groomer having her head split open in front of him.

Does this absolve him of fault? No. But it is muddied enough that he's also a victim, and one that I can't help but want to see where he'll get by the end of all of this.

And the only real crime he did before is heavily hinted to have been initiated by his "victim", and maybe even kept going by her as well, while he was more or less a husk of having his groomer having her head split open in front of him.
Does this absolve him of fault? No. But it is muddied enough that he's also a victim, and one that I can't help but want to see where he'll get by the end of all of this.

So now Touka can enter the church...

Awhile back Yaus denied several people entering the Cathedral: Otoha, Touka, and Imai. Her reasoning is that certain conditions for these people have not been met (though Yaus was majorly answering Otoha, I feel like this would apply to the other two that didn't get in), and these people wouldn't be able to even see the church without the presence of others who unknowingly completed their rites of passage.

If entering church or not has less to do with "what activities will be done inside the church" but is simply a global check on "whether this girl has met the conditions or not", that means that Touka went from missing the bar during Halloween wars to meeting the bar during Chapter 4 in the eyes of HOPE. So what are those conditions? And are all girls sharing the same set of conditions?

The most evident recent change to Touka is of course having her bad taste in man fully exposed, but it's hard to say whether or not Touka bore those feelings toward Sensei already during Halloween wars (and it's very likely she was already fawning over him during those times according to all the slightly flirty interactions). In addition, Imani, who likely fell for Akira as soon as they started working together, was also denied entry at the time. Thus despite the fact that feelings can be loosely applied to all girls that are allowed to enter, it either isn't the right condition for Imani, or simply isn't the right angle to look at this (which is more possible).

Honestly I don't think something like I like you is enough to pass HOPE's identity check, but for now I cannot remember what other "new" things about Touka that make her worthy of participating the surreal part of Kumon-mi. Back then it was more straightforward to theorize why Rin and Sana were granted passage, but I have a hard time coming up with a reason that's spicy enough for Touka to come in

As for Nodoka and Kaori, just.......c'mom in I guess since you two are so weird that denying your entry sounds even weirder.

Here is my theory dump about Kaori, John, Sekai, and the Wire God. This post is very long, so proceed at your own risk. (And sorry if I'm repeating any old analysis here, but it's really difficult to search an 1850-page thread for discussion of old events.)

My basic thesis is that Wires has been fighting against Sekai's attempts to take control of Kaori, and one of the ways he has acted is through John (until he lost that power around the end of winter), but there are still some things that confuse me.

First, starting with Kaori. In the Chapter 3 main event "First Contact" Kaori says she has three parts: regular human parts, her heart, and "tubes and wires":


Her heart (along with her other organs) presumably refers to the influence of Sekai, and thus it would make sense for the "tubes and wires" to refer to the Wire God. But why does Kaori have "wire parts"? And where does Pareidolia fit into this? Let's look back at how Kaori described her accident and the hospital:
She equates the hospital with "evil robots" and describes how she had to escape. The robots point toward Wires (I think she described the hospital with mechanical imagery elsewhere as well, but I've lost track of it), and Wires is also connected to life support in regards to Mr. Tojo. My interpretation: Wires was responsible for saving Kaori after the accident, but she "escaped" before the "treatment" was complete. As for what caused the escape, she links it to the birth of a baby spider and to the "mistress of the dark," indicating Pareidolia's influence. She also indicates the spider didn't exist until "that day" (probably of the accident, but could also be the day of the escape) - my money is on Pareidolia being linked to Sekai's organs (which she also received "that day").

A few other indications that her organs are connected to Pareidolia and dislike Tojo Ramen/the Old District:
"Black Sandy Beaches"

"A Short List"


"Wither"

And now for something that confuses me: in her Chapter 1 event "Objects and Appendages," Kaori says some things about overcoming the world:

The mention of concern and the Queen of Spiders points towards Pareidolia, which led to my initial interpretation that Pareidolia thinks (knowing the guy, probably incorrectly) that he has gained control over the Sekai that is inside Kaori. But John says something extremely similar in "Såsom i en Spegel":
And I'm convinced that he's not talking for Pareidolia there. To explain why, let me talk about John for a bit.

First, regarding birds and chickens in general. Kaori indicates chickens are Pareidolia's enemies:
Yasu has said that birds are sacred to Hope:
But this in regards to "bird Maya," and if she is aligned with any of the trinity, it's Wires. There's also a clear connection between birds and Wires with Tsuneyo's love of birds and Noodles being her "son," and she seems to associate chickens in particular with her father. Furthermore, the narrator in "All For You" seems to equate cicadas, spiders, and birds with the trinity, which would mean birds stand in for Wires:

John is first introduced in "Mysterious Abundance of Chickens" after Sekai speaks through Kaori for the first time:



Sensei collapses, Hope starts monologuing about Sekai's accident and the danger of memories, and some text appears on screen (from Sekai? from Pareidolia? somehow both?):

Then Wires shows up (is this the first time he appears outside of a happy event?) and it's implied that he's able to do something that prevents a Sensei "brain melt"/total reset. When Sensei wakes up, Kaori says John saved him:

So Wires saves Sensei and Kaori sees John save Sensei, an immediate indication that Wires could be acting through John. One other thing to note: before collapsing, Sensei is not able to understand the chickens, so Wires could have given him that ability when he fixed things.

Moving now to "Såsom i en Spegel," there are additional indications that John is speaking for Wires. Kaori suggests Sensei's ability to understand him is due to a god:

John warns Sensei he will lose his "eyes," probably referring to Wires guiding his vision:

John seems concerned about the coming return of summer, and thinks he is "not long for this world" (Because he will lose the ability to communicate? Or he is speaking for Wires himself, who is about to disappear?):


John makes a warning about a dead God who is going to return:

This could refer to Hope, who is asleep for winter, but I think it's almost certainly about Pareidolia. Pareidolia has been "dead" (waiting for his season) for at least thousands of years, and his return is accomplished with the death of Maya Prime (due to Sensei's "incorrect choice" of not sacrificing someone else). Furthermore, the title of the event points to Pareidolia: Såsom i en Spegel is the original-language title of Ingmar Bergman's Through a Glass Darkly. In that film's climax, a schizophrenic woman sees God in the form of a spider. (Off topic aside: the film also has a scene of implied incest between an approximately 30-year-old and a teenager, both of whom have psychiatric issues )

John also warns about Maya's festival, suggesting he's worried about what's going to happen to her:

John is then interrupted as he loses the ability to communicate, with these being his final words:
Which are a Caesar cipher for
"not yet no no no no!"
"not in front of her!"
"not before she [REDACTED]"
I have no idea what he's about to say, would love to hear theories. In any case, John's communication ability is abruptly lost (possibly Wires losing connection?). I believe DeSkel15 has suggested that the timing syncs up with Wires disappearing until Chapter 4, but I haven't confirmed that.

So if we return to John's lines about "conquering the world" under the assumption that he speaks for Wires, one interpretation is that John/Wires has "conquered" the Sekai within Kaori, but will eventually lose the fight with the end of winter and Sekai's upcoming restoration. But I'm not sure why Pareidolia (through Kaori) and Wires (through John) use such similar language.

One more throwaway line that might connect John to Wires (refer back to Kaori's "tubes and wires"):

Assuming a John/Wires connection, there is one event that confuses me, which is when he briefly shows up in Wakana's Chapter 2 event "Soup, or Another Year Without You":



The capitalization in "my Father" suggests a god, so he could be talking for Wires again, but the word choice ("servants" and "Father") suggests Hope to me. It's also strange that he's apparently not talking in "chicken-speak" here, even though this event happens before "Såsom i en Spegel" so he should still have the ability to be understood (and what has John "made known to us" before "Såsom i en Spegel"?).

OK, enough about John, time to discuss Kaori again. In "Wither," Kaori mysteriously dissappears after the Tojo Ramen power goes out, which in other events has been connected to Wires losing power. I don't have a great explanation for this, but here's a plausible one: Wires has been protecting Kaori from SeKaori. When the power goes out, that protection is weakened and SeKaori takes control. She wants to get out of Wires's place of power before he's able to reinstall the protections, so she teleports away with Pareidolia's help.

Protections from Wires against SeKaori might also be indicated in "Run, Rabbit, Run" when she takes control to kiss Sensei. In the middle of this, Kaori briefly regains control, but after a visual glitch loses control again:

Other instances of this glitch correspond to Wires losing connection. It could be happening here when SeKaori overcomes Wires to reassert control. (Side question: any ideas what 4349 means?)

In the most recent Kaori events, it's suggested that Kaori has "deer parts," referring to the Sekai inside of her. Ami tells a story in which doctors in a hospital want to remove the deer parts (i.e. Wires wants to get rid of the Sekai possession):



In "Tree Village" Kaori is looking for a "color machine" and reveals that she will use it to change people's colors (including getting rid of Sensei's current "darkness," i.e. Pareidolia):
She says her own colors are green on the outside and red on the inside (the red being Sekai):
Wires is associated with machinery, and he also shows up during the treasure hunt to reveal the mystery door to Sensei and Nao-chan. It seems like Kaori (with Wires's help or under his direction) wants to use the color machine to remove her "inner red," i.e. get rid of SeKaori. This is supported by the poem at the beginning of Nao's event "Silver Tongue," in which Sekai says a "color wheel" won't be able to remove her:

One last piece of speculation: Kaori says that Frog Boy (human frog) is absorbing John's "chicken powers," will protect us from "the darkness" (Pareidolia), and will be involved in using the color machine. Sounds to me like Wires has a new avatar.


To summarize, Wires has been fighting to protect Kaori from SeKaori. For his motive, I can think of a few possibilities:
1. Wires is a god of maintaining order and correcting errors, and he sees SeKaori as an error.
2. SeKaori is allied with Pareidolia and Wires wants to prevent him from gaining strength.
3. Wires could want Kaori for his own purposes. I have the beginnings of a batshit crazy theory in regards to this, but I'll probably need to finish a second playthrough before I have enough info to write about it. Stay tuned!

tl;dr: The Wire God possesses the largest cock in Kumon-mi and has been using it to dominate Sekai.

Spoiler:
To Die, To Sleep
She equates the hospital with "evil robots" and describes how she had to escape. As for what caused the escape, she links it to the birth of a baby spider and to the "mistress of the dark," indicating Pareidolia's influence. Spoiler
"Black Sandy Beaches"
"A Short List"
"Wither"

Spoiler
The mention of concern and the Queen of Spiders points towards Pareidolia, which led to my initial interpretation that Pareidolia thinks (knowing the guy, probably incorrectly) that he has gained control over the Sekai that is inside Kaori. But John says something extremely similar in "Såsom i en Spegel":
Spoiler
And I'm convinced that he's not talking for Pareidolia there. To explain why, let me talk about John for a bit.
First, regarding birds and chickens in general. Kaori indicates chickens are Pareidolia's enemies:
Spoiler:
Mysterious Abundance of Chickens
Yasu has said that birds are sacred to Hope:
Spoiler:
The Legacy of Thaum Pt. IV
But this in regards to "bird Maya," and if she is aligned with any of the trinity, it's Wires. There's also a clear connection between birds and Wires with Tsuneyo's love of birds and Noodles being her "son," and she seems to associate chickens in particular with her father. Furthermore, the narrator in "All For You" seems to equate cicadas, spiders, and birds with the trinity, which would mean birds stand in for Wires:
Spoiler
John is first introduced in "Mysterious Abundance of Chickens" after Sekai speaks through Kaori for the first time:
Spoiler
Sensei collapses, Hope starts monologuing about Sekai's accident and the danger of memories, and some text appears on screen (from Sekai? from Pareidolia? somehow both?):
Spoiler
Then Wires shows up (is this the first time he appears outside of a happy event?) and it's implied that he's able to do something that prevents a Sensei "brain melt"/total reset. When Sensei wakes up, Kaori says John saved him:
Spoiler
So Wires saves Sensei and Kaori sees John save Sensei, an immediate indication that Wires could be acting through John. One other thing to note: before collapsing, Sensei is not able to understand the chickens, so Wires could have given him that ability when he fixed things.
Moving now to "Såsom i en Spegel," there are additional indications that John is speaking for Wires. Kaori suggests Sensei's ability to understand him is due to a god:
Spoiler
John warns Sensei he will lose his "eyes," probably referring to Wires guiding his vision:
Spoiler
John seems concerned about the coming return of summer, and thinks he is "not long for this world" (Because he will lose the ability to communicate? Or he is speaking for Wires himself, who is about to disappear?):
Spoiler
John makes a warning about a dead God who is going to return:
Spoiler
This could refer to Hope, who is asleep for winter, but I think it's almost certainly about Pareidolia. Pareidolia has been "dead" (waiting for his season) for at least thousands of years, and his return is accomplished with the death of Maya Prime (due to Sensei's "incorrect choice" of not sacrificing someone else). Furthermore, the title of the event points to Pareidolia:
Såsom i en Spegel
is the original-language title of Ingmar Bergman's
Through a Glass Darkly
. In that film's climax, a schizophrenic woman sees God in the form of a spider. (Off topic aside: the film also has a scene of implied incest between an approximately 30-year-old and a teenager, both of whom have psychiatric issues
)
John also warns about Maya's festival, suggesting he's worried about what's going to happen to her:
Spoiler
John is then interrupted as he loses the ability to communicate, with these being his final words:
Spoiler
Which are a Caesar cipher for
"not yet no no no no!"
"not in front of her!"
"not before she [REDACTED]"
I have no idea what he's about to say, would love to hear theories. In any case, John's communication ability is abruptly lost (possibly Wires losing connection?). I believe
DeSkel15
has suggested that the timing syncs up with Wires disappearing until Chapter 4, but I haven't confirmed that.

Spoiler:

Spoiler

But this in regards to "bird Maya," and if she is aligned with any of the trinity, it's Wires. There's also a clear connection between birds and Wires with Tsuneyo's love of birds and Noodles being her "son," and she seems to associate chickens in particular with her father. Furthermore, the narrator in "All For You" seems to equate cicadas, spiders, and birds with the trinity, which would mean birds stand in for Wires:
Spoiler
View attachment 3705674
John is first introduced in "Mysterious Abundance of Chickens" after Sekai speaks through Kaori for the first time:
Spoiler
View attachment 3705678
View attachment 3705680
View attachment 3705683
View attachment 3705684
Sensei collapses, Hope starts monologuing about Sekai's accident and the danger of memories, and some text appears on screen (from Sekai? from Pareidolia? somehow both?):
Spoiler
View attachment 3705688
View attachment 3705689
Then Wires shows up (is this the first time he appears outside of a happy event?) and it's implied that he's able to do something that prevents a Sensei "brain melt"/total reset. When Sensei wakes up, Kaori says John saved him:
Spoiler
View attachment 3705692
View attachment 3705693
So Wires saves Sensei and Kaori sees John save Sensei, an immediate indication that Wires could be acting through John. One other thing to note: before collapsing, Sensei is not able to understand the chickens, so Wires could have given him that ability when he fixed things.
Moving now to "Såsom i en Spegel," there are additional indications that John is speaking for Wires. Kaori suggests Sensei's ability to understand him is due to a god:
Spoiler
View attachment 3705695
View attachment 3705696
John warns Sensei he will lose his "eyes," probably referring to Wires guiding his vision:
Spoiler
View attachment 3705697
View attachment 3705707
John seems concerned about the coming return of summer, and thinks he is "not long for this world" (Because he will lose the ability to communicate? Or he is speaking for Wires himself, who is about to disappear?):
Spoiler
View attachment 3705712
View attachment 3705714
View attachment 3705716
John makes a warning about a dead God who is going to return:
Spoiler
View attachment 3705717
View attachment 3705718
This could refer to Hope, who is asleep for winter, but I think it's almost certainly about Pareidolia. Pareidolia has been "dead" (waiting for his season) for at least thousands of years, and his return is accomplished with the death of Maya Prime (due to Sensei's "incorrect choice" of not sacrificing someone else). Furthermore, the title of the event points to Pareidolia:
Såsom i en Spegel
is the original-language title of Ingmar Bergman's
Through a Glass Darkly
. In that film's climax, a schizophrenic woman sees God in the form of a spider. (Off topic aside: the film also has a scene of implied incest between an approximately 30-year-old and a teenager, both of whom have psychiatric issues
)
John also warns about Maya's festival, suggesting he's worried about what's going to happen to her:
Spoiler
View attachment 3705720
John is then interrupted as he loses the ability to communicate, with these being his final words:
Spoiler
View attachment 3705721
Which are a Caesar cipher for
"not yet no no no no!"
"not in front of her!"
"not before she [REDACTED]"
I have no idea what he's about to say, would love to hear theories. In any case, John's communication ability is abruptly lost (possibly Wires losing connection?). I believe
DeSkel15
has suggested that the timing syncs up with Wires disappearing until Chapter 4, but I haven't confirmed that.
So if we return to John's lines about "conquering the world" under the assumption that he speaks for Wires, one interpretation is that John/Wires has "conquered" the Sekai within Kaori, but will eventually lose the fight with the end of winter and Sekai's upcoming restoration. But I'm not sure why Pareidolia (through Kaori) and Wires (through John) use such similar language.
One more throwaway line that might connect John to Wires (refer back to Kaori's "tubes and wires"):
Spoiler:
In Regard to the Peony
View attachment 3705739
Assuming a John/Wires connection, there is one event that confuses me, which is when he briefly shows up in Wakana's Chapter 2 event "Soup, or Another Year Without You":
Spoiler
View attachment 3705740
View attachment 3705741
View attachment 3705743
View attachment 3705744
The capitalization in "my Father" suggests a god, so he could be talking for Wires again, but the word choice ("servants" and "Father") suggests Hope to me. It's also strange that he's apparently not talking in "chicken-speak" here, even though this event happens before "Såsom i en Spegel" so he should still have the ability to be understood (and what has John "made known to us" before "Såsom i en Spegel"?).
OK, enough about John, time to discuss Kaori again. In "Wither," Kaori mysteriously dissappears after the Tojo Ramen power goes out, which in other events has been connected to Wires losing power. I don't have a great explanation for this, but here's a plausible one: Wires has been protecting Kaori from SeKaori. When the power goes out, that protection is weakened and SeKaori takes control. She wants to get out of Wires's place of power before he's able to reinstall the protections, so she teleports away with Pareidolia's help.
Protections from Wires against SeKaori might also be indicated in "Run, Rabbit, Run" when she takes control to kiss Sensei. In the middle of this, Kaori briefly regains control, but after a visual glitch loses control again:
Spoiler
View attachment 3705746
View attachment 3705747
Other instances of this glitch correspond to Wires losing connection. It could be happening here when SeKaori overcomes Wires to reassert control. (Side question: any ideas what 4349 means?)
In the most recent Kaori events, it's suggested that Kaori has "deer parts," referring to the Sekai inside of her. Ami tells a story in which doctors in a hospital want to remove the deer parts (i.e. Wires wants to get rid of the Sekai possession):
Spoiler:
Il Cervo
View attachment 3705751
View attachment 3705891
View attachment 3705757
In "Tree Village" Kaori is looking for a "color machine" and reveals that she will use it to change people's colors (including getting rid of Sensei's current "darkness," i.e. Pareidolia):
Spoiler
View attachment 3705759
She says her own colors are green on the outside and red on the inside (the red being Sekai):
Spoiler
View attachment 3705761
Wires is associated with machinery, and he also shows up during the treasure hunt to reveal the mystery door to Sensei and Nao-chan. It seems like Kaori (with Wires's help or under his direction) wants to use the color machine to remove her "inner red," i.e. get rid of SeKaori. This is supported by the poem at the beginning of Nao's event "Silver Tongue," in which Sekai says a "color wheel" won't be able to remove her:
Spoiler
View attachment 3705762
One last piece of speculation: Kaori says that Frog Boy (human frog) is absorbing John's "chicken powers," will protect us from "the darkness" (Pareidolia), and will be involved in using the color machine. Sounds to me like Wires has a new avatar.
Spoiler:
Tree Village
View attachment 3705766
View attachment 3705767
To summarize, Wires has been fighting to protect Kaori from SeKaori. For his motive, I can think of a few possibilities:
1. Wires is a god of maintaining order and correcting errors, and he sees SeKaori as an error.
2. SeKaori is allied with Pareidolia and Wires wants to prevent him from gaining strength.
3. Wires could want Kaori for his own purposes. I have the beginnings of a batshit crazy theory in regards to this, but I'll probably need to finish a second playthrough before I have enough info to write about it. Stay tuned!

One question, is the Eternum game really good or is it just an overrated game? As I'm going to have to wait another 25 days for LIL, I feel like killing time with something, so I wanted to know if you recommend the game or not and if not, which games you recommend.
Click to expand...
I didn't like it. It's been some time, and from my list I gave it a 2/10 playing it at 0.6 - however I don't remember much of it. I think I sort of remember the story being kind of interesting and the girls being hot, but something about the game design just made it too much for me. I tried to power-through with a guide, but just ended up giving up since I wasn't that hooked in the story either.

I'll add some recommendations since I've been putting it off until now.
Unfortunately my top recommendations in terms of story are all in rpgm format. Last Sovereign would be the obvious choice, great story (deconstructs the hero genre) and would take even more time than LiL in just the amount of planning you must make in order to get what you want from every big event (or you could just cheat the amount of resources and that will help with half of it). It's free on steam and nearing its final update.

Demon Roots is an interesting story about the battle between demons and humans, but it's actually about demons being more humane than the human empire - and it's a finished game. But it has many weird turns both in mechanics and overall story choices.

Renryuu Ascension brings many interesting things to the table in terms of kingdom building and an astounding harem number (and the author's obssession with virginity) - however it's way way way far from being completed. You should have some closure at least in the sense that it closes up a big arc of the story.

I recommend you cheat as much as you can in all of these games cause honestly rpgm is something I have to suffer in order to experience these stories rather than something I enjoy.
I'll start by listing a few with stories that will take you some time to finish and aren't that recommended generally.

Monster Girl 1000 (completed) is about a world where the birth of men is almost gone, and guess who can solve that with his penis? Despite its start, it has a surprisingly interesting lore as you approach the middle of the story, but falls flat in the final arc. Like really flat. But hey, it's a completed game and you get to have sex with a 1000 girls (not really, it's at most 100).

Love & Sex: Second Base (completed) is the sims with a main quest about transforming every girl in town into a fucktoy. Or it could be, since you can just marry one of them and finish the game too. Or many of them, there are several harems. You need to keep checking the wiki for this one, but good game overall.

HushHush (completed) is an interesting story about a time loop involving a couple of girls - which will all die without your intervention. The ending is somewhat shallow though, and the author's intention of enabling whatever gender for the player makes the sex scenes weird, since there is sex happening but no mc representation (since it has to account for both penis and no penis).

Superhuman was an interesting story about a dude being infected by a parasite with a sort of mystery angle, but I felt that it lost itself as it becomes more and more of a generic hero academy plot. It is a long story though.

These all fall into that umbrella of either being famous or a "generic dude builds a harem in sandbox": Randel Tales, Goddesses Whim, Champion of Realms, Corrupted Kingdoms, Unveiling the Unknown (completed), Harem Hotel, World Tamer, Hero's Harem Guild, Lewd Town Adventures, Inn Another World, My Girlfriend's Friends, Aurelia, Parasite Black, Being a Dik, Zombie Girl's Island (completed), Love and Corruption, Shuggerlain.

There are slave trainers/corruption stories: Elven Conquest 1 and 2 (completed), Realms of Bondage, Hero Party Must Fall, Monster Girl Club Bitfrost (completed), Strive for Power (completed), Masters of Raana, One Room (completed).

This is the only one on the list where you're being corrupted instead (as a wife that starts to fall for your student), but it's well done: Turning the Page.

And these are just bizarre games, but all of them are complete. The reason I add them is for the case-study of the author's vision conflicting with narrative sense:

Home & Dungeon (completed) is a wholesome city-builder that for some reason has you resorting to rape the people that would happily have sex with you in a consensual way.

Roundscape: Adorevia (completed) is a harem builder with no narrative cohesion. For instance, girls will fall in love with you, but still jump at the opportunity to have sex with anything that moves. The author will give you an option to "disable" the NTR/sharing, but that just means that the mc will walk away while it's happening - and then say that it just isn't possible for that to be NTR because you're not in a relationship with any of them (why add the option then lol).
If you give in and start replaying LiL instead though, please remember to pay attention to the colors that appear (especially green, red, blue and white) and the moons since it's still unclear if that was a thing from the start (or since when it was a thing).

While most RPG maker games (eroge) are utter trash, those two, og and sequel are gems.

Alice Soft RGP eroge.

Story is great.
No animations and made in anime style cgs.

posts.content_html_raw: If there is one game i wish i could convince more people to try it would be NSFW Wrestling. Yes, on the face of it i can see plenty of reasons for folks to dismiss it but under the cover is a great story with a well written cast of lovable and quirky characters. This isn't a WWE wrestling game, it's more like a story from the backstage of a theatre company and it's a real fuckfest on top of being a fun story. Yes, there is sharing content, but it's avoidable if it really isn't something you can handle though i would recommend trying it at least purely because, i found the MC to be almost impossible to project on to, so it's not you sharing girls, it's more like watching a large group of people banging for fun and cause they're good friends, and family, lots of incest, like, so much incest... there's no netorare cuck-play or anything, that's not at all what the game is aiming for or striving for and as i said, it's all able to be disabled, along with the couple of futa characters. Fire Lord Zuko said:
Sensei - “THAT ISN’T TRUE! STOP MAKING ME DO THINGS TO PEOPLE WHO DON’T DESERVE THEM!”
Pareidolia- “Fine, fine. Jeez.”
- “I’ll just have to find someone who does."
Click to expand...
That part about him finding someone that does had always flew under my radar and I'm now scared.

Although, granted, if there is someone in this cast that Io would probably respect in terms of trauma that someone is Akira. I don't believe in trauma olympics, but if we were to compare the damage their respective traumas did to the world as a whole, or rather, what their inability to deal with their traumas did, Akira wins by such a landslide it's not even comparable.
Io was abused by her mother and that forced her aunt to become her guardian and she's a bitch in general to people.

Akira suffered from severe psychosis, probably lost his father to it, was neglected by his mother (at the least), was religiously brainwashed to an extent (in fact Sekai saying she believed in god to Ami might be because of the Arakawa family too), was abused by a mother/teacher figure, groomed for a decade, was never able to escape into Niki and thus affected her life as well, ntr'd in his own house, most likely had to deal with the doubt of Ami being his kid as a teenager, witnessed said love of his life getting her head torn open in front of him and dragged her body himself, had to become a guardian to her/his daughter while dealing with his resurfaced psychosis, had no family at all to rely on other than a kid, became a criminal/Sekai through his relationship with Maya and thus negated all possibility of claiming himself as a mere victim in his tragedy, was then probably abused/blackmailed in some level by Maya - and we haven't reached the resets yet nor have I mentioned all 30-40 people heavily affected by him.

All that just to say that even if the worst happens, as long as Akira at least opens up to Io about a fraction of all of this, there may be a hail mary in the sense that she might do a Sara and go with it until the episode stops. I mean, she said she considered at one point taking one for the team while heavily medicated...
That might be all heavy wishful thinking, but I don't see another angle through which she gets assaulted and survives this mentally other than her accepting it beforehand in regards to his mind being broken/having an episode. And for all Io's attitude makes me don't really care about her, I don't want to see her broken or assaulted either.

Edit: It would be funny if all of our predictions turn wrong and the scene is super uplifting with Io going "damn, you've been through some heavy shit too, huh? Maybe we can heal and face our fears together - who even cares about brattydolia".

posts.content_html_raw:
Moonflare said:
I didn't like it. It's been some time, and from my list I gave it a 2/10 playing it at 0.6 - however I don't remember much of it. I think I sort of remember the story being kind of interesting and the girls being hot, but something about the game design just made it too much for me. I tried to power-through with a guide, but just ended up giving up since I wasn't that hooked in the story either.

I'll add some recommendations since I've been putting it off until now.
Unfortunately my top recommendations in terms of story are all in rpgm format. Last Sovereign would be the obvious choice, great story (deconstructs the hero genre) and would take even more time than LiL in just the amount of planning you must make in order to get what you want from every big event (or you could just cheat the amount of resources and that will help with half of it). It's free on steam and nearing its final update.

Demon Roots is an interesting story about the battle between demons and humans, but it's actually about demons being more humane than the human empire - and it's a finished game. But it has many weird turns both in mechanics and overall story choices.

Renryuu Ascension brings many interesting things to the table in terms of kingdom building and an astounding harem number (and the author's obssession with virginity) - however it's way way way far from being completed. You should have some closure at least in the sense that it closes up a big arc of the story.

I recommend you cheat as much as you can in all of these games cause honestly rpgm is something I have to suffer in order to experience these stories rather than something I enjoy.
I'll start by listing a few with stories that will take you some time to finish and aren't that recommended generally.

Monster Girl 1000 (completed) is about a world where the birth of men is almost gone, and guess who can solve that with his penis? Despite its start, it has a surprisingly interesting lore as you approach the middle of the story, but falls flat in the final arc. Like really flat. But hey, it's a completed game and you get to have sex with a 1000 girls (not really, it's at most 100).

Love & Sex: Second Base (completed) is the sims with a main quest about transforming every girl in town into a fucktoy. Or it could be, since you can just marry one of them and finish the game too. Or many of them, there are several harems. You need to keep checking the wiki for this one, but good game overall.

HushHush (completed) is an interesting story about a time loop involving a couple of girls - which will all die without your intervention. The ending is somewhat shallow though, and the author's intention of enabling whatever gender for the player makes the sex scenes weird, since there is sex happening but no mc representation (since it has to account for both penis and no penis).

Superhuman was an interesting story about a dude being infected by a parasite with a sort of mystery angle, but I felt that it lost itself as it becomes more and more of a generic hero academy plot. It is a long story though.

These all fall into that umbrella of either being famous or a "generic dude builds a harem in sandbox": Randel Tales, Goddesses Whim, Champion of Realms, Corrupted Kingdoms, Unveiling the Unknown (completed), Harem Hotel, World Tamer, Hero's Harem Guild, Lewd Town Adventures, Inn Another World, My Girlfriend's Friends, Aurelia, Parasite Black, Being a Dik, Zombie Girl's Island (completed), Love and Corruption, Shuggerlain.

There are slave trainers/corruption stories: Elven Conquest 1 and 2 (completed), Realms of Bondage, Hero Party Must Fall, Monster Girl Club Bitfrost (completed), Strive for Power (completed), Masters of Raana, One Room (completed).

This is the only one on the list where you're being corrupted instead (as a wife that starts to fall for your student), but it's well done: Turning the Page.

And these are just bizarre games, but all of them are complete. The reason I add them is for the case-study of the author's vision conflicting with narrative sense:

Home & Dungeon (completed) is a wholesome city-builder that for some reason has you resorting to rape the people that would happily have sex with you in a consensual way.

Roundscape: Adorevia (completed) is a harem builder with no narrative cohesion. For instance, girls will fall in love with you, but still jump at the opportunity to have sex with anything that moves. The author will give you an option to "disable" the NTR/sharing, but that just means that the mc will walk away while it's happening - and then say that it just isn't possible for that to be NTR because you're not in a relationship with any of them (why add the option then lol).
If you give in and start replaying LiL instead though, please remember to pay attention to the colors that appear (especially green, red, blue and white) and the moons since it's still unclear if that was a thing from the start (or since when it was a thing).
Click to expand...
What’s the hype of Last Sovereign about? I quit by the time I recruited the sister because the game is just too unforgiving and requires the players to follow a guide to the dot. Started over 3 times by then, once because I didn’t kill the early enemies which caused my characters to be too weak, second time to strip the early characters off their equipment since the enemies were still way too strong and money making opportunities too limited to waste it on something that turns out to be the ‘wrong’ thing, third time because I recruited the sister after defeating enemies in the cave and house. It’s mandatory to know about every single detail in advance and follow a predetermined order you won’t know about until you failed and ought to repeat the last 45 minutes.

I thought these pseudo sandbox games like LiL are stupid for expecting players to repeat scenes hundreds of times in pursuit of the new events, but that game really took the cake

Slub said:
What’s the hype of Last Sovereign about? I quit by the time I recruited the sister because the game is just too unforgiving and requires the players to follow a guide to the dot. Started over 3 times by then, once because I didn’t kill the early enemies which caused my characters to be too weak, second time to strip the early characters off their equipment since the enemies were still way too strong and money making opportunities too limited to waste it on something that turns out to be the ‘wrong’ thing, third time because I recruited the sister after defeating enemies in the cave and house. It’s mandatory to know about every single detail in advance and follow a predetermined order you won’t know about until you failed and ought to repeat the last 45 minutes.

I thought these pseudo sandbox games like LiL are stupid for expecting players to repeat scenes hundreds of times in pursuit of the new events, but that game really took the cake
Click to expand...
It is perhaps Sierra's only real shortcoming as a dev imo, her games are strict, complicated and filled with traps to trip up cheating, but if you can force your way past that or carefully work your way around the traps, the stories are really quite solid. I found the most straightforward way to cheat around 99% of the combat bullshit was to use the rpgmakersaveedit.exe to add bonus stats to any combat characters, it certainly took care of the worst of the difficulty, the rest was just carefully reading the guide to allocate the right points during the major events. It's not for everyone though, you've gotta put the work in to get to the story unfortunately.

The hype, as you asked, is twofold imo: The gameworld and story heavily changes based on your decisions (which are by themselves very complex and far-reaching as months and years go by), and the story itself which is very interesting.

As for mechanics, I'm sure that many people enjoy it, but for me personally, as someone that sucks in most games of this genre, I simply cheat my characters/party to have maximum health, money and pron (investment money) - as I play for the story and consider rpgm mechanics themselves to be an obstacle to it. What you said about the guide is correct though, this either requires you to follow a guide and choose your path based on it or have some unexpected consequences even with cheating.

Kind of the same approach I have to LiL in that regard, since I try my utmost to ignore the game design by every means possible. Granted that LiL requires a lot less messing around - you just have to follow the guide mod and fish for the reset answers.

Bingoogus said:
It is perhaps Sierra's only real shortcoming as a dev imo, her games are strict, complicated and filled with traps to trip up cheating,
Click to expand...
If I remember correctly she has deployed two anti-cheating mechanisms, one in the form of a level you aren't supposed to get to (since there is no grinding in this game), and the other around a character that you wouldn't be able to beat/or able to beat in x turns... It turned out not being that convoluted, but one should look for it in the guide just in case. Also I personally find this anti-cheating silly in regard to single-player games, but what can you do...
